title: A city that put its own centre back together
episode: Resilient Warsaw - Rick Steves' Europe Travel Bite
description: American travel writer Rick Steves on how Warsaw, about 85 per cent destroyed by 1945, rebuilt itself. Castle Square, with King Sigismund III’s column and the reconstructed Royal Castle, is where the rebuilt Old Town begins.

title: Monuments to the fighters of 1944
episode: Warsaw, Poland: Heroes, Memorials, and Restoration
description: Rick Steves looks at how Warsaw remembers its dead and rebuilt its streets. The Warsaw Uprising Monument on Krasiński Square, unveiled in 1989, shows insurgents climbing down into the sewers they used to move between districts.

title: Chopin, and the national spirit
episode: Warsaw, Poland: Vodka and Chopin - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide - Travel Bite
description: Rick Steves on two Polish passions, vodka and the composer Fryderyk Chopin, who grew up in Warsaw and left for Paris in 1830. The Chopin Museum in the Ostrogski Palace holds his last piano and manuscripts.

title: Daffodils for the ghetto fighters, eighty years on
episode: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising commemorated on 80th anniversary
description: In April 1943 Jewish fighters in the Warsaw Ghetto, the walled district where the Nazis confined the city’s Jews, rose against deportation to Treblinka. BBC News reports on the 2023 commemoration at the Monument to the Ghetto Heroes in Muranów.
